Reference / mail/message

mail/message#

E-mail messages (RFC 5322 with MIME): built, rendered, parsed.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let message = MailMessage(
    from: "Ada <ada@example.test>",
    to: ["Grace <grace@example.test>"],
    subject: "Lunch on Thursday?",
    text: "Shall we try the new place?\r\n",
);
message.bytes();                                 // wire form, CRLF
message.string();                                // for reading, \n
let back = ParsedMail(bytes).message();
back.headers().first("Subject");

Description#

E-mail messages (RFC 5322 with MIME): built, rendered, parsed.

MailMessage(from:, to:, subject:, text:) adds Date, a fresh Message-ID, MIME-Version and a UTF-8 Content-Type. Text beyond ASCII, or with a line longer than 998 octets, goes out quoted-printable, which every transport carries (RFC 2045 §6.7); other text stays 7bit. A message knows nothing of the SMTP envelope; DeliveredMail is the copy to hand to a server, without Bcc.

MailMessage(from: "Ada ada@example.test", to: ["grace@example.test"], subject: "Lunch?", text: "Shall we?"): Date is now, Message-ID is fresh and the body is UTF-8 text, quoted-printable when it is not ASCII or has a line over 998 octets. clock: and random: fix them, as tests do.
